title: Resting cells are spherical; the amoeboid phase is one of activity and unequal tensions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Resting cells are spherical; the amoeboid phase is one of activity and unequal tensions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In naked protoplasmic cells the amoeboid form marks a phase of activity with unequal surface tensions, whereas the spherical form marks a phase of rest when internal homogeneity and minimal potential energy are attained, at which time the cell also becomes encysted.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In the case of the naked protoplasmic cell, as the amoeboid phase is emphatically a phase of freedom and activity, of chemical and physiological change, so, on the other hand, is the spherical form indicative of a phase of rest or comparative inactivity.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Surface tension in protoplasm and amoeba”. Scope: naked protoplasmic cells, amoebae and other protists with resting stages

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The morphological and activity association is directly measurable in time-lapse data. Public records can test it in selected protists, but the tension mechanism and broad generality remain only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track individual amoeboid cells through active, resting, and encysting phases; quantify sphericity, motility, biochemical activity, and cortical-tension uniformity. Support requires consistent rounding and reduced activity before or during encystment, with active phases showing asymmetric tension and form.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sphericity can reflect wall formation rather than equilibrium.

Cell state labels and tension measurements are rarely both present.

Some resting cells remain nonspherical or do not encyst.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The activity-versus-shape association is a straightforward classification and can be attempted on published protist images. Those images are not a designed sample, and rest is sometimes defined by roundness, which weakens the test. The tension mechanism is an extra claim that the images do not carry.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify naked cells by activity state and by shape, and test whether active cells are amoeboid while resting or encysted cells are spherical. That association would support the descriptive claim; active spheres or resting amoeboid forms at high frequency would refute it. Unequal surface tension as the cause of the amoeboid phase needs a separate tension measurement.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Activity and 'rest' are often inferred from the shape being explained.

Images are anecdotal relative to a survey of naked cells.

Encystment adds a wall, so sphericity need not be a tension minimum.

analysis feasibility: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.65
data existence: 0.4
